sourceV3.Annotation_Format: Dense pixel-level annotations [Claude] | Pixel-level GT masks [Claude] | Frames grouped by class [Claude] | Image folders by surface and quality class; exact file format NR [GPT]
sourceV3.Annotation_Source: Manual dense annotation [Claude] | Manual annotation [Claude] | Frame extraction and manual class assignment [GPT]
sourceV3.Annotation_Quality_Control: Peer-reviewed publication (Autonomous Robots) [Claude] | Class-specific counts reported; independent label QC NR [GPT]
sourceV3.Reported_AI_Tasks: Segmentation; Classification [Claude] | Semantic segmentation;Road surface classification [Claude] | Classification;Road surface type and condition recognition [Claude] | Classification;Road-surface quality recognition [GPT]
sourceV3.AI_Task_Evidence: Reported on the source record/data card or associated publication (see Evidence_Locator)
sourceV3.Key_Limitations: Very low resolution (352x288) limits fine crack detection; only 701 annotated images; captured exclusively in good weather and daylight, so it cannot support robustness testing under rain, low light or glare; collection dates not reported [Claude] | Damage classes are part of a broader surface-type taxonomy; data hosted on external LAPIX/UFSC site (link liveness not independently re-tested) [Claude] | No licence declared, which is the main barrier to reuse; Image_Count is recorded as NR because the per-class frame list is cut off mid-sentence on the record - the six visible counts (asphalt Good 1,978; asphalt Regular 839; asphalt Bad 464; paved Regular 324; paved Bad 124; unpaved Regular 796) total 4,525 but at least the unpaved-Bad count is missing, so no total can be stated; condition grades are ordinal image-level labels, not engineering condition indices; no per-frame GPS [Claude] | Kaggle class counts sum to 5,118 frames, while a later publication reports 6,264 images; image count is therefore UNK. No PCI, IRI, GPS, or sensor synchronization is reported. [GPT]
